key_insight: This paper shows that judging AI agents only by task success misses what users actually care about: values like autonomy, dependability, affordability, bounded reach, reviewability, and equitable access. By analyzing real Reddit discussions about OpenClaw, the authors reveal a practical value framework for understanding everyday agent use.
problem_solved: AI agent evaluations usually focus on whether the task was completed, but they often ignore user values, tradeoffs, and negative experiences. This paper addresses the gap between performance metrics and the human values that shape real-world trust and adoption.
method: Analyzed 73,093 first-person Reddit posts about OpenClaw use.
Used Value Sensitive Design plus LLM-assisted coding to label each post by human value, agent aspect, value fulfillment, and user outcome.
Grouped 21 identified values into 6 broader value categories to build a structured view of user priorities.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper provides a more human-centered evaluation lens for agent design and benchmarking. It can help teams build agents that are not just effective, but also trustworthy, affordable, controllable, and aligned with everyday user expectations.
visual_elements: A 6-part value wheel or taxonomy showing the six value groups.
A pipeline diagram: Reddit posts -> LLM-assisted coding -> value groups -> insights.
A comparison chart contrasting task-completion metrics vs. value-sensitive evaluation.
Icon set for key values such as autonomy, trust, cost, control, and fairness.
paper_title: Value-Sensitive Delegation in Everyday AI Agent Use: Evidence from OpenClaw
paper_authors: Renkai Ma, Ruyuan Wan, Xuan Lu, Fan Yang, Chen Chen
